bib.title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning

question: Can a single convolutional network trained with a Q-learning variant learn control policies for Atari games directly from raw pixels?
hypothesis: Deep learning's success on raw sensory input can carry over to RL if experience replay is used to handle correlated data and a shifting data distribution.
contributions: A CNN (DQN) trained end to end from raw pixels with Q-learning and SGD
Q-learning with experience replay and minibatch updates
One architecture and hyperparameter set across seven Atari games, state of the art on six

method.summary: A CNN with one output per action estimates Q from the last 4 preprocessed frames. It is trained online with RMSProp on minibatches sampled uniformly from a replay memory, with epsilon-greedy behaviour, on seven ALE games.

datasets.name: Arcade Learning Environment: Beam Rider, Breakout, Enduro, Pong, Q*bert, Seaquest, Space Invaders
datasets.split: no train/test split; trained and evaluated per game
datasets.preprocessing: RGB to gray-scale, downsample to 110x84, crop 84x84 playing area; stack last 4 frames; rewards clipped to +1/-1 in training only; frame skip k=4 (k=3 on Space Invaders)

models.name: DQN
models.architecture: CNN: conv 16 8x8 stride 4 + ReLU; conv 32 4x4 stride 2 + ReLU; FC 256 ReLU; linear output per action (4 to 18 actions)
models.init_from: inferred: random weights, from Algorithm 1 'Initialize action-value function Q with random weights'

training.objective: Squared TD error (y - Q(phi,a;theta))^2, y = r + gamma max_a' Q(phi',a';theta), y = r at terminal; previous-iteration parameters fixed in the loss (Eq 2-3)
training.wall_clock: Fig 2 caption: one epoch is 50000 minibatch weight updates or roughly 30 minutes of training time

other.epsilon: annealed linearly 1 to 0.1 over first million frames, then 0.1
other.frame_skip: k=4, k=3 on Space Invaders (the only per-game difference)

other.eval_steps: 'a fixed number of steps', value not stated; Fig 2 uses 10000 steps

metrics.name: average total reward per episode
metrics.definition: Total game score per episode averaged, from epsilon-greedy 0.05 policy run for a fixed number of steps

metrics.name: average max predicted Q
metrics.definition: Mean over a held-out set of states (collected by a random policy before training) of max_a Q

baselines: HNeat Best and HNeat Pixel (Hausknecht et al. 2013)
Human expert (median reward after about two hours of play)
eval.protocol: Single run per game as reported; no seeds, variance or significance test stated. HNeat and DQN Best are single best episodes.

limits: Learning rate, gamma, RMSProp decay and number of evaluation steps are not stated.
Only seven games; DQN is far below human on Q*bert, Seaquest, Space Invaders (long-horizon strategies).
Reward clipping cannot distinguish reward magnitudes.
Uniform replay sampling and overwriting with recent transitions ignore transition importance; authors suggest prioritized sweeping.
No convergence guarantees; stability shown empirically only.
Human scores are the authors' own and are much higher than those in Bellemare et al.
No target network (introduced in the later Nature version).

code.snippet: Deep Q-learning with Experience Replay: store (phi_t,a_t,r_t,phi_t+1) in D; sample random minibatch; y_j = r_j (terminal) or r_j + gamma max_a' Q(phi_j+1,a';theta); gradient step on (y_j - Q(phi_j,a_j;theta))^2
